newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary APV evaluates bids for MHB, decision soon.
newsitem.headline: Hungary APV evaluates bids for MHB, decision soon.

text.p: A committee of Hungary's privatisation agency APV has evaluated the bids for a majority stake in MHB bank, and the winner is likely to be chosen soon, APV Managing Director Istvan Abel told Reuters on Thursday.
"We have valid bids," Abel said. "The committee, which decides if the bids are valid and evaluates them in a points system, has held its session today and prepared its proposal."

According to press reports, Austria's Creditanstalt- Bankverein and the Dutch ABN Amro Bank NV submitted bids in the one-round tender for the sale of an 89.23 percent stake in MHB, Hungary's fifth largest bank.

Abel said tender rules did not allow him to disclose further information, but added that APV's soon-to-be appointed board of directors was likely to make its decision about the sale at its first session.
The previous APV board was sacked along with Minister of Industry and Trade Tamas Suchman three weeks ago over a scandal concerning irregular payments to an adviser and is still to be replaced.
The government said it was likely to appoint the new board at its session later on Thursday.
Abel said MHB's sale was likely to be completed this year.
He said if the new board of directors were not named soon, it would be logical if the government itself made the final decision on the winner of the tender.
"We could more or less settle the controversial points, and the situation is fairly unambiguous," he said.
